inlines.value: Python, R, Julia, and Rust API extraction
Diplodocus reads configured API targets and uses native tooling to complete
language semantics and verify documentation examples. Rust extraction invokes
Cargo and rustdoc, including local compilation and build scripts. Other adapters
require callers to prepare compiled packages beforehand. Diplodocus does not
install dependencies. Targets must point to maintained files inside
their declared package and repository boundaries. The
Rust extraction uses Cargo and rustdoc to document the compiler-selected public
API, including reexports from private modules, macro-generated declarations,
generic signatures, traits, associated items, and implementations. Crate and
module documentation appear alongside item documentation. Hidden items stay out
of the public reference. Type and trait pages group their fields, variants,
methods, and implementations under stable anchors.
Declare one explicit library entry file:

blocks.source:
[[package]]
id = "eunoia"
name = "Eunoia"
slug = "rust"
ecosystem = "rust"
repository = "eunoia"
path = "crates/eunoia"
metadata-path = "Cargo.toml"
targets = [
  { id = "api", extractor = "rust", path = "src/lib.rs", role = "public-api" },
]

Shared help topics retain all documented usages and arguments on each
declaration's page. Topic aliases resolve to a primary declaration, while
method aliases resolve to their own pages. Links between declarations and
methods grouped by S3 class make the complete topic navigable.

topic's primary declaration. The reference overview lists each topic with its

buttons. Usage appears once, including the complete shared topic's signatures.
